chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Umar ibn al-Khattab was brought a slave girl against whom they had testified that she had committed adultery. And part of her story was that she was an orphan with a man, and the man used to be frequently absent from his family. So the orphan girl matured, and the wife feared that her husband might marry her. So she called women until they restrained her, and she took her virginity with her finger. So when her husband returned from his absence, the wife accused the orphan girl of immorality and established proof from her neighbors who had aided her in doing so.

That was raised to Umar, but he did not know how to judge regarding her. Then he said to the man, 'Go to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and we will go with you to him.' So they came to Ali (peace be upon him) and related the story to him. He said to the wife of the man, 'Do you have proof or evidence?' She said, 'There are witnesses for me, these neighbors of mine who testify against her with what I am saying,' so she presented them.

So Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) brought out the sword from its sheath and placed it in front of him, and ordered that each one of them enter a room. Then he called the wife of the man and interrogated her from every aspect, but she refused to waver from her words. So he returned her to the room in which she was, and called one of the witnesses, and sat on his knees. Then he said, 'Do you recognize me? I am Ali ibn Abi Talib, and this is my sword. The wife of the man has said what she said. If you return to the truth, I will give you amnesty; and if you are not truthful to me, I will fill the sword with your blood.' So she turned to Umar and said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! The amnesty is for me.' So the Commander of the Faithful said to her, 'So speak the truth.'

She said, 'No, by Allah, except that she saw beauty and a good figure in her, so she feared the ruin of her husband upon her. So she gave her an intoxicating drink, and called us, so we restrained her, and she deflowered her with her finger.'
So Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'Allah is the Greatest! I am the first to differentiate between the two witnesses, except for Daniel the Prophet.'

So Ali necessitated upon the woman the legal penalty of the slanderer, and necessitated upon all of them together the dower, and made her dower to be four hundred dirhams. And he ordered that the woman be separated from the man, and her husband divorce her, and he married the girl to him, and Ali (peace be upon him) paid the dower from himself.

So Umar said, 'O Abu al-Hasan! Narrate to us the story of Daniel.' So Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed, Daniel was an orphan, having no mother for him nor a father, and a woman from the Children of Israel, an old woman, took him in and raised him.'

And a king from the kings of the Children of Israel had two judges for him, and they had a friend who was a righteous man, and he had a beautiful, lovely wife, and he used to come to the king and discuss with him.

And the king had a need to send a man in one of his matters, so he said to the two judges, 'Choose a man to send him in one of my matters.' So they said, 'So and so.' So the king sent him. So the man said to the two judges, 'I bequeath to you both regarding my wife for her safety.' So they said, 'Yes.' So the man went out.

So the two judges used to come to the door of the friend, so they desired his wife and enticed her to give herself to them, but she refused. So they said to her, 'By Allah, if you do not do it, we will testify against you in the presence of the king with adultery, then we will have you stoned.' So she said, 'Do whatever you both like.' So they went to the king and informed him, and testified in his presence that she had committed adultery. So a great matter entered the king because of that, and his grief over her intensified, and he was admiring her.

So he said to them, 'Your words are accepted, but stone her after three days.' And he called out in the city in which he was, 'Attend the killing of so-and-so the worshipper, for she has committed adultery, for the two judges have testified against her with that.' So the people were many regarding that, and the king said to his vizier, 'What do you have regarding this from a stratagem?' He said, 'I have nothing regarding that.'

So the vizier went out on the third day, and it was the last of her days, and he saw naked boys playing, and among them was Daniel, and he did not know him. So Daniel said, 'O group of children! Come, until I am the king, and you be so-and-so the worshipper, and so-and-so and so-and-so be the two judges testifying against her.'

Then he gathered dust and made a sword from a reed, and said to the boys, 'Take this one by the hand and move him to such and such a place, and take this one by the hand and move him to such and such a place.'

Then he called one of them and said to him, 'Speak the truth, for if you do not speak the truth, I will kill you.' And the vizier was standing, watching and listening. So he said, 'I testify that she committed adultery.' He said, 'When?' He said, 'On such and such a day.' He said, 'Return him to his place and bring the other one.' So they returned him to his place and brought the other one. So he said to him, 'With what do you testify?' He said, 'I testify that she committed adultery.' He said, 'When?' He said, 'On such and such a day.' He said, 'With whom?' He said, 'With so-and-so, son of so-and-so.' He said, 'And where?' He said, 'At such and such a place.'

So one of them contradicted his companion. So Daniel said, 'Allah is the Greatest! They testified with falsehood. O so-and-so, call out among the people that these two testified against so-and-so with falsehood, so present them and kill them.' So the vizier went to the king quickly and informed him of the news. So the king sent for the two judges, and they differed just as the two boys had differed. So the king called out among the people and ordered with their killing.

key_terms.حَدَّ الْقَاذِفِ: The legal penalty for the slanderer

ai.seo_question: How did Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) use witness examination to prove a false adultery accusation?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights Ali ibn Abi Talib’s judicial acumen in distinguishing between true and false witnesses (*al-farq bayn al-shahidayn*) by exposing the mistress's fabrication of the girl's virginity to prevent her marriage. Ali explicitly links his method to the Prophet Daniel’s (*Dhaniel*) use of children to uncover discrepancies in testimony, establishing a precedent for using psychological insight in legal proceedings. This narrative underscores the Shia emphasis on the infallible Imam’s ability to discern truth through divine inspiration and logical deduction.
